QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_64

question.text: SAS-1300 distinguishes 'access' from 'usage'. Which metric BEST captures USAGE (not just access)?

answer.text: Average monthly transactions per account, deposits-to-withdrawals ratio, digital-payment frequency (UPI transactions per user per month)

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Usage-indicators: transaction frequency, deposit behaviour, digital-payment activity per user per month. Access indicators (accounts, ATM cards, branches) don't tell you whether the inclusion is real. **The Trap:** Options A, C, B are access / supply-side indicators. **Cross-Exam Context:** Access-vs-usage distinction echoed in V-A (MF Distributor — SIP continuation) and V-B (MF Foundation). **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** A zero-transaction active bank account is worse than a 100-transaction informal one. Under SAS-1300, always measure usage-activity alongside access-coverage.
